rows.text: The plan is the same every turn: attack with a one-mana creature nobody can block, wait for blockers to be declared, then swap it out for something enormous that is already through. Ninjutsu and sneak both do this, and the commander pays you a card and a permanent +1/+1 counter every time any of it connects. The cheap unblockable bodies are not filler — they are the engine.

rows.name: Heroes in a Half Shell
rows.text: 5/5 vigilance, menace, trample, haste, and every combat damage step where your Mutants, Ninjas or Turtles connect puts a counter on ALL of them and draws you a card. Five colours is the cost; it is worth it.

rows.name: Roaming Throne
rows.text: name Ninja. Every Ninja damage trigger in the deck fires twice — two cards off Ingenious Infiltrator, two off Ninja of the Deep Hours, two commander triggers.

rows.name: Silver-Fur Master
rows.text: ninjutsu costs {1} less, and every other Ninja and Rogue gets +1/+1. It makes the cheap enablers into real threats.

rows.name: Splinter, Hamato Yoshi
rows.text: another Ninja anthem on a menacing body that can itself be sneaked in.

rows.name: Changeling Outcast
rows.text: one mana, cannot block, cannot BE blocked, and it is every creature type — so it triggers the commander too.

rows.name: Mist-Cloaked Herald
rows.text: one mana, unblockable.

rows.name: Slither Blade
rows.text: the third copy.

rows.name: April O'Neil, Kunoichi Trainee
rows.text: scries two on entry and cannot be blocked by anything with power three or more.

rows.name: Prehistoric Pet
rows.text: unblockable by anything bigger, and it taps to bounce another creature you control — a free ninjutsu enabler that does not need combat.

rows.name: Faerie Seer
rows.text: flies, scries two.

rows.name: Mothdust Changeling
rows.text: every type, and it can give itself flying by tapping a spare creature.

rows.name: Inkrise Infiltrator
rows.text: flies, and pumps when you have mana spare.

rows.name: Ornithopter
rows.text: free, flies, and it is a perfectly good ninjutsu enabler on turn one.

rows.name: Smoke Shroud
rows.text: flying on anything, and it climbs back out of the graveyard every time a Ninja enters.

rows.name: Cover of Darkness
rows.text: name Ninja. Fear on the whole team means almost nothing can block them.

rows.name: Fallen Shinobi
rows.text: two free cards off their library on every hit. The best raw payoff in the deck.

rows.name: Ingenious Infiltrator
rows.text: a card for EVERY Ninja that connects, not just itself. With three attackers that is three cards.

rows.name: Ninja of the Deep Hours
rows.text: a card per hit for two mana.

rows.name: Moon-Circuit Hacker
rows.text: a card per hit, with no discard on the turn it arrives.

rows.name: Higure, the Still Wind
rows.text: tutors the next Ninja on every connection, and makes any Ninja unblockable for {2}.

rows.name: Nashi, Moon Sage's Scion
rows.text: exiles the top card of every library and lets you cast one, paying life instead of mana.

rows.name: Prosperous Thief
rows.text: a Treasure whenever any Ninja or Rogue connects — which pays for the next ninjutsu.

rows.name: Mistblade Shinobi
rows.text: bounces a blocker or a problem permanent every hit.

rows.name: Kappa Tech-Wrecker
rows.text: exiles an artifact or enchantment on connection.

rows.name: Sakashima's Student
rows.text: a copy of the best creature on the board, and it is a Ninja on top.

rows.name: Satoru, the Infiltrator
rows.text: draws whenever creatures enter WITHOUT being cast. Ninjutsu does not use the stack as a cast, so every single ninjutsu activation draws a card.
Sneak works like ninjutsu but is a discounted CAST — the creature enters tapped and attacking after blockers.

rows.name: Raphael, the Nightwatcher
rows.text: attacking creatures have double strike. Every damage trigger in the deck fires twice.

rows.name: Michelangelo, Improviser
rows.text: puts a creature AND a land from your hand onto the battlefield on every hit.

rows.name: Donatello, Gadget Master

rows.text: lifelink, and it grows on every point of life you gain.

rows.name: Dark Leo & Shredder
rows.text: attacking Ninjas gain deathtouch, and with five Ninjas out its damage halves an opponent's life.

rows.name: Mikey & Don, Party Planners
rows.text: lets you play lands and cast Mutants, Ninjas and Turtles straight off the top of your library, with a bonus counter.

rows.name: Don & Raph, Hard Science
rows.text: their attack makes your next noncreature spell cost one less per artifact.

rows.name: Raph & Leo, Sibling Rivals
rows.text: untaps attackers and grants an ADDITIONAL COMBAT PHASE. Two rounds of ninjutsu triggers per turn.

rows.name: Mikey & Leo, Chaos & Order
rows.text: a card the first time each turn you put a counter on a creature — which the commander does every combat.

guide.title: Turning the connections into a kill

rows.name: Shredder, Shadow Master
rows.text: attacks one player and makes a tapped attacking copy at each other opponent. Every copy that connects halves that player's life. Two swings ends the table.

rows.name: Dark Leo & Shredder
rows.text: the second halving effect, live as soon as you have five Ninjas.

rows.name: Sphere Grid
rows.text: a counter on every creature that connects, and everything with a counter gets reach and trample.

rows.name: Bident of Thassa
rows.text: a card for every creature that connects, and it can force the table to attack each other.

rows.name: Dolmen Gate
rows.text: your attackers take no combat damage at all. Attack with everything, every turn, for free.

rows.name: Heroic Intervention
rows.text: hexproof and indestructible through the wrath this deck is most afraid of.

rows.name: Continue?
rows.text: returns up to four creatures that died this turn straight back to the battlefield. It is the answer to a blocked alpha strike or a wrath in combat.

rows.name: Cyclonic Rift
rows.text: overloaded, it clears every blocker for a lethal ninjutsu turn.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Kappa Tech-Wrecker
rows.text: repeatable artifact and enchantment removal on a body.

rows.name: Rhystic Study
rows.text: their turns pay for yours.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise
rows.text: turn-one fixing, and it flies, so it is also a ninjutsu enabler.

rows.name: Bloom Tender
rows.text: with a five-colour commander down it taps for a lot.

rows.name: Chromatic Lantern
rows.text: makes every land produce every colour, which is what a WUBRG commander needs.

rows.name: Farseek
rows.text: fetches any shockland with a basic type.

rows.name: Nature's Lore
rows.text: an untapped Forest-typed dual.

rows.name: Ninja Pizza

rows.name: Prosperous Thief
rows.text: Treasures off combat, which is the deck's most reliable ramp.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a one-mana unblockable creature. Changeling Outcast, Mist-Cloaked Herald or Ornithopter on turn one means a real Ninja is on the battlefield by turn two, and the deck simply does not function without that opener.
Ninjutsu AFTER blockers are declared, not before. The whole point is that the creature you return was already unblocked, so the Ninja arrives already through. Sneak works the same way.

rows.name: Heroes in a Half Shell
rows.text: five specific colours is a real cost, so do not hold the whole hand waiting for her. The Ninja package wins games on its own; she makes it draw twice as many cards when she lands.

rows.name: Roaming Throne
rows.text: name Ninja, not Turtle. The Ninjas carry the repeatable damage triggers; the Turtles are mostly static effects that the Throne would not double anyway.
